text:
maria chen: Quick sync — we need a final, reproducible bench protocol for quantized runs that accounts for KV cache and batching effects. I sketched something in a doc but want a short checklist we can run as a harness.

devin: +1. main pain points: warmup token sequences, power-capping GPU, tokenizer detokenization differences, and measuring cache hit/miss impact.

samir: Proposed checklist:
- fixed seed + deterministic tokenization (use sentencepiece model v3) 
- single-request warmup: send 2x sequence-length tokens for 5 iterations to populate KV
- steady-state warmup: run 30s of continuous generation at target concurrency
- sku power cap: record perf at default, 200W, 150W (use nvidia-smi --power-limit)
- compare kernels: FP16, FP8, INT8, 4-bit (same graph, only quant ops swapped)
- measure: latency p50/p95, throughput (tokens/s), GPU util, memory, KV hit rate

leo: Add: record batching statistics (avg batch size, queue latency) and disable/enable dynamic batching to compare. Also log batching heuristic decisions (why a request was in its batch).

ash: For KV cache behavior, do two experiments:
1) cold-start: no KV warmup, random prompt each time
2) hot-path: warmup once, then run many similar prefixes to measure cache amortization
Record cumulative token cost and per-token latency.

maria chen: Love that. Also want a short CLI we can run. Draft command:
```
./bench_runner --model redwood-xl-8k --precision int8 --tokenizer spm_v3.model \
  --warmup-cold 5 --warmup-steady 30 --concurrency 8 --duration 300 \
  --measureings [latency,throughput,gpu,caching] --power-caps 250,200,150
```

devin: Two notes: 
- ensure we pin model weights and kernel selection via env var `RW_KERNEL_PREF=auto|int8|4bit` so runs are comparable
- flush OS pagecache and restart runtime between precision runs to avoid residual state

samir: On calibration effects: include a calibration-only run where we run the calibration dataset (1000 prompts) and then benchmark without retraining. Compare speed and output quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LL) for small eval set.

leo: For fairness across precisions, also normalize batch packing: enforce same token-per-batch budget e.g., 4096 tokens per batch and same max gen length. Otherwise quantized runs benefiting from different batching will skew results.

ash: Perf-bot note: I ran an FP8 vs INT8 spot test on staging yesterday and saw a 12% throughput win for FP8 but a 3% higher p95. Saved logs to s3://redwood-perf/quickshots/2026-03-xx-fp8-int8.json

maria chen: Next steps: can someone produce a one-page checklist + bench_runner wrapper that implements these flags? Aim to run across 3 models and upload traces. I'll use results to decide kernel defaults. If anyone has objections to the warmup durations call them out now.

devin: I'll implement bench_runner and add an option `--kv-warmup-mode=[none,single,steady]`. Will push WIP by EOD.

samir: I'll assemble calibration dataset and the evaluation scripts for quality metrics. Also add a profiler hook so we can attribute time to quant kernels vs copy/pack.

leo: I'll add logging to the batching heuristic to emit why it chose the batch size (e.g., TTL, backlog, token budget).

perf-bot: scheduled job created: perf/quant-protocol/1772456789 -> runs on staging in 24h. Results will be posted to #eng-platform and S3.

maria chen: Thanks team. If you hit weird KV anomalies (e.g., stale keys after precision switch) post them here. :rocket:
